title: GpuLock.__enter__ opens the lock fd but __exit__ does not run if the body raises — fd leak on exception in the guarded command
detail: Run 2026-06-22T22-42-41 (error-handling-gpu_monitor-407, low) re-confirmed with a sharper framing: GpuLock.__enter__ opens the lock fd but only closes it for 3 narrow exception types; unexpected exceptions leak the fd+process reference. The context-manager protocol guarantees __exit__ only on normal exit or exceptions RAISED WITHIN the with-block, not on failures between fd-open and block-entry. Fix shape: open the fd inside a try/finally in __enter__, or ensure __enter__ is exception-safe (close the fd on ANY failure before returning self). Same resource-lifetime class as mlx-review:image-open-without-context-manager but for the GPU lock fd. Run 2026-06-23T11-52-18 (correctness-gpu_monitor-407, low) re-confirmed with a sharper framing: GpuLock fd is opened before the flock loop; advisory detect_gpu_busy runs each poll but the real mutex is flock (no race), BUT the fd is not closed on BaseException — confirming the exception-safety gap persists. Run 2026-06-23T14-01-20 (FIX tier, type-safety-gpu_monitor-400, low) APPLIED the typing facet: added `from typing import IO` + annotated `self._lock_fd: IO[str] | None = None` in GpuLock.__init__ — the fd-leak-on-exception itself REMAINS unfixed (the type annotation only documents the leak, does not close it).

title: SeedVR2 single-step Euler math hardcodes t=1000/s=0 — adversarial REJECT: multi-step schedules would need re-derivation, not a latent bug for the current single-step path

title: Promoting the multi-LoRA list->scalar peel into a typed shared helper first_or(values, default) in _shared.py — canonical reusable fix for the list-vs-scalar family
detail: Run 2026-06-22T22-42-41 (FIX tier, type-safety-image-workflow-876/872): the recurring multi-LoRA list->scalar peel (`lora_path[0] if isinstance(lora_path, list) and lora_path else default`) was ad-hoc at each call site (image-faceswap:394, video-relay:1018, video-vbvr:364). title: RunConfig.from_json now runs a post-construction type-coercion pass — closes the argparse-default-None vs typed-dataclass gap without changing behavior
detail: Run 2026-06-22T22-42-41 (FIX tier, type-safety-run_config-322 + 128 + 277): RunConfig.from_json loaded raw JSON values into typed dataclass fields with NO validation/coercion, and RunConfig.cfg_scale is annotated float (non-Optional) while the argparse default is None. APPLIED: added _coerce_typed_fields() — a post-construction pass that introspects the dataclass field annotations (handles BOTH string-form 'int'/'float'/'Optional[int]' AND runtime typing.Union/UnionType), normalizes string/numeric values, skips non-numeric and bool fields, preserves None on Optional fields, raises explicit ValueError on null-in-non-Optional and bad coercions. LESSON: the dataclass-from-JSON boundary is the canonical place for a coercion pass — it closes the type gap WITHOUT changing behavior semantics (so no test-contract regression, unlike the `or`-fallback removal). Prefer type-narrowing-only fixes over behavior-semantic changes to stay restore-safe (see gotcha:sysexit-to-exception-breaks-assert-tests).

title: A variable assigned inside an if-branch is referenced in the else-branch (or after the if without a prior-branch default) — NameError at runtime, masked when the defining branch is the common path
detail: Run 2026-06-23T11-52-18 (FIX tier, argparse-integrity-image-profile.py-830, HIGH): image-profile.py referenced `resolved_lora` in the else (zimage) branch but it was only defined inside the use_flux2 branch. The NameError is masked in normal runs that take the defining branch; it detonates only on the alternate path. APPLIED: hoisted the `resolved_lora` assignment above the if/else so BOTH branches share the binding. GENERAL LESSON: when a variable is used in multiple branches of an if/else (or after the block), define it in a scope visible to ALL consumers — assign a default before the if, or hoist the assignment above the block. The bug-class is invisible to tests that only exercise the defining branch; audit both branches when a variable is branch-local. Sibling to the branch-coverage-blindspot family.

title: Distilled model generate() unconditionally overwrites explicit cfg_scale/stg_scale to fixed values — silent feature-disable for distilled variants
detail: Run 2026-06-23T14-01-20 (correctness-ltx_pipeline-329, medium): app/ltx_pipeline.py:329 — the distilled generate() path unconditionally sets cfg_scale=1.0 / stg_scale=0.0, overwriting ANY explicit user value passed via --cfg-scale/--stg-scale. Sibling to mlx-review:cfg-scale-literal-compare-sentinel + mlx-review:or-pattern-overrides-zero, but distinct: this is not a sentinel-compare bug, it is an UNCONDITIONAL assignment that ignores the user's explicit value entirely. The distilled path legitimately needs cfg=1.0/stg=0.0 (CFG is inert for distilled models per MEMORY flux2-klein-cfg-inert-when-distilled), but the unconditional overwrite means a user CANNOT override even when they know their distilled variant benefits from a non-default value. Fix shape: only overwrite when the user did NOT explicitly pass the flag (use the default=None sentinel check), not unconditionally. Unfixed this run. NOTE: this is the video-pipeline sibling of the FLF2V auto-override family — both are distilled-model CFG overrides, both need the sentinel-discriminated fix.
